g.text: ADR-005: Data sources in stages: registry, list, evidence
How do trials get from a registry into TrialWatch so that a person chooses what to read, every source works the same way, and a check never runs on
what forces this decision now: facts and constraints, no solutions
• A sync took EU CT numbers a person typed and fetched each trial's record and documents in one step. CTIS was the only source with code; which documents to fetch
• CTIS lists 12,905 trials (POST /search, up to 500 per request): the whole list takes about 30 requests. The evidence does not: a record and its PDFs are several
requests per trial at one per second, then the page text must be read.
• A check that reads a trial whose documents did not all arrive, or could not be read, would call missing evidence "not reported": a false accusation.
• Other registries (ClinicalTrials.gov) and trials entered by hand must fit the same flow. Nothing is in production: one current config per source, runs log the
2–3 real options; the current proposal is only one of them
How it works: a person pastes EU CT numbers; a sync
fetches the record and the documents and reads their
pages; checks run on whatever has pages.
• no view of what a source holds
• a partly failed sync still looks ready for a check
How it works: core.source names the adapter that
reads a source and holds its config (what to list,
what evidence to transfer). Syncing the list makes
every listed trial a trial here (key, title,
identifiers). Transferring evidence fetches a chosen
trial's record and configured documents and reads
their pages, recorded as complete or failed. Checks
• browse and choose before paying for downloads
• the whole list is stored before any trial is read
C. Live search, sync what is ticked
How it works: the web interface searches CTIS live;
the trials ticked there are synced in one step, as
• still no completeness check before a check
+ better · 0 no difference · – worse, and a few words why
Quality: checks read all the evidence
– a missing PDF reads as absent
Effort: to build and to maintain
Traceability: why a trial came in
Undo: how hard to reverse later
what we chose and which criteria decided it
We choose B: every source is registered with an adapter and a config, and trials come in in two stages; a check runs only on a trial whose evidence came in
completely. B is the only option that keeps checks off missing evidence (risk, quality) and records why each trial came in (traceability).
1. Registry: core.source gains adapter (code in src/trialwatch/sources/registry.py), enabled and config (jsonb, checked by the adapter). CTIS: listing.criteria
(its search fields) and page_size; evidence.document_kinds. Manual is a source with no list.
2. Sync the list (`source sync`): page through the source's list in key order; each trial is matched by its key and identifiers, or created; core.source_listing
keeps its title, the day the source last changed it and the listed row. A complete pass marks the trials no longer listed (kept).
3. Transfer evidence (`source transfer`): for chosen trials (keys, or pending / failed / stale / listed): the record, the configured documents and their page
text. core.evidence_transfer says complete, or failed and why. Stale: the source changed the trial since; still checkable, and shown.
4. Only complete trials are checked: evidence.run, the CLI and the web interface refuse the others (core.ready_trials). A trial entered by hand is complete once
5. Both stages are ingest runs (kind list or transfer) that log the config they used; a job can be stopped between trials. `ctis sync` is gone.
Easier: choosing trials from the whole registry; a new registry is one adapter
class; seeing per trial what is missing or stale; trusting that a checked trial
Harder: the list brings ~13,000 trials in before any is read (pages are paged);
one PDF that fails blocks the trial's check until a transfer gets it.
Revisit when: a source has no list (list it from a file); lists should sync on a
schedule; one unreadable PDF should not block a check of the others.
Lab: tests sync a fake CTIS list, transfer, stop, go stale, fail a download and
refuse a check; a real sync of CTIS's whole list is next.
Decided with the user on 2026-11-21: syncing a source means getting its list of trials (id, name) mapped into our trials; evidence is transferred as each source's
config says; checks run only on trials whose evidence was transferred (downloaded and read). The live-search page (C) was proposed first and dropped.
Amended 2026-11-21 after a code review: stale evidence no longer counts as checkable (a sponsor's corrected document would be judged by its old copy). A check reads
a trial only when every source that holds it has a complete, current transfer that brought the document kinds the check reads; a stale trial is transferred again first (sources/stages.py, not_ready).
How to use: copy to docs/adr/ADR-NNN-name.excalidraw · replace the grey text (set it to black) · status chip colour: orange open, yellow proposed, green accepted, grey
superseded · one page: if it doesn't fit, the decision is too big, so split it.
